record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Clarify the physical meaning of off-forward or skewed parton distributions measured in deeply virtual Compton scattering. Although these generalized distributions extend parton distribution functions away from the forward direction and can be measured with considerable effort, the open question is what they are heuristically and what hadron properties will be learned by measuring them.

evidence.quote: What can “off-forward” parton distributions tell us about hadron properties?
What is missing so far, to my taste, is a heuristic understanding of the physical significance of off-forward parton distributions.
We still need to figure out exactly what they are and what will we learn by measuring them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Off-forward (a.k.a. skewed or generalized) parton distributions (GPDs) extend the ordinary parton distribution functions of a hadron to nonzero momentum transfer between the incoming and outgoing hadron states. For a nucleon they are defined as off-diagonal matrix elements of bilocal light-cone quark and gluon operators,

  F^q(x, ξ, t) = ∫ (dz⁻/4π) e^{i x P⁺ z⁻} ⟨P'| q̄(−z/2) γ⁺ q(z/2) |P⟩ |_{z⁺=z_⊥=0},

(and analogous structures for helicity-flip, gluon, and tensor operators), where P, P' are the initial/final hadron momenta, ξ is the skewness measuring the longitudinal momentum transfer, and t = (P' − P)² is the invariant momentum transfer. Such distributions enter the amplitude for hard exclusive processes, most notably deeply virtual Compton scattering γ*(q) N(P) → γ(q') N(P').

Problem. Provide a heuristic physical interpretation of the off-forward parton distributions F^q(x, ξ, t) (and their gluon and helicity-dependent analogues) as intrinsic properties of a hadron, and identify precisely which hadron-structure observables—e.g., transverse spatial parton densities, orbital angular momentum contributions to the nucleon spin, energy-momentum tensor form factors, or other dynamical quantities—are determined by these distributions. In particular, characterize:

(a) the position-space content of GPDs (for example, via Fourier transform in transverse momentum transfer at ξ = 0);
(b) the relation of their Mellin moments to local matrix elements of the QCD energy-momentum tensor and the resulting decomposition of nucleon spin into quark/gluon angular momentum;
(c) what new, model-independent information about the internal structure of the nucleon is obtained from measurements of deeply virtual Compton scattering and related hard exclusive reactions that is not contained in ordinary parton distribution functions or elastic form factors.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made since the question was posed. Burkardt's impact-parameter interpretation (GPDs at ξ=0 as transverse spatial parton densities) and Ji's sum rule (linking the second Mellin moment of GPDs to the quark/gluon contribution to nucleon spin and to energy-momentum tensor form factors, including pressure and shear distributions) provide a well-established heuristic picture, and DVCS experiments at HERMES, JLab, COMPASS and (planned) the EIC continue to map them out. However, a fully model-independent extraction (the "deconvolution problem") remains unsolved, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Deconvolution problem of deeply virtual Compton scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses unresolved model-independent extraction of GPDs from DVCS observables.
status_evidence.claim: Model-independent reconstruction of GPDs from DVCS data is still an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Generalized parton distributions (Physics Reports review)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive review explaining the physical interpretation of GPDs and their links to hadron structure.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic physical interpretation of GPDs (transverse imaging, Ji sum rule, energy-momentum tensor) has been substantially developed.

status_evidence.title: DVCS and GPDs topic summary
status_evidence.snippet: GPDs reveal three-dimensional hadron structure and the energy-momentum tensor of the nucleon via DVCS.
status_evidence.claim: GPDs give access to 3D nucleon structure, parton orbital angular momentum, and gravitational form factors.
